rationale: Both are table-driven and correct. B is more uniform: its comments slice covers every verse, including the fly ending and the horse line, so Verse is one straight path with a single check for the first and last verses, and the closing fly line is reused from the table. A's comments map includes an entry for verse 8 that is never used, because the switch hardcodes "She's dead, of course!" again. A also writes out the fly ending twice and uses an index-keyed map where a slice would be simpler. B's one weakness is that its spider case hardcodes the whole line instead of adding the extra clause the way A does, which repeats some text. B also has doc comments on its exported functions and A has none. Overall B has less duplication and is better documented.
